searchText: Hello, is there a geth fork that already uses verkle trees? if yes where can I find it? I think this is the PR to follow <https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/25253> Is there an EIP set for verkle trees the PR says it includes all the EIPs also is Cancun the verkle trie testnet? I think it would only be referring to: <https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/verkle_tree_eip> I think the most recent one is called Condrieu oh okay, time to go down in the rabbit hole are you looking for something in particular? just looking on how to implement them as an EL dev just started diving I want to make Erigon sync to Condrieu as a first start Which parts are you looking to implement from scratch (If any)? not from scratch, I want to port verkle trees on Erigon so how to convert hashed state => verkle root basically I read some articles for an high level overview but without a deep dive Ah I see, yeah I think you mainly want to look at the section in the EIP named Tree-embedding and beyond, the implementation details before that are hidden behind the verkle libraries, so you will mainly need to acknowledge that the insert interface for verkle is `insert(key : 32bytes, value : 32bytes)` ooooh, I assume that key is hashed address, and value is either hashed account or hashed storage value well, I would also like a deep dive because, why not It would be good to know exactly what questions you have in mind regarding integrating verkle tries into a client, so they can be collected into a FAQ I will think about some of them is there a verkle tree C++ library already? if there is not, then I will try writting one Not that I'm aware of Mmmmh okay, I think I can start writting one, after I am done deep diving the Silkworm Team will need one eventually If you do C++ then have bindings for it as IIRC Nethermind is using Rust bindings right now so that would be helpful yeah, that is the intention, if you want to use it like that it is okay Silkworm is written in C++ so they need some native stuff Before you dive into a C++ lib if you want get familiar a CI action or similar is still needed to test parity among the implementations So Go/Python/Rust/etc can all be assured to function the same I never adopted CI I can do that later, now it is time for studying why can you not use Rust binding BTW? Rust is as efficient as C++ AFAIK also Rust is better IMO as a language overall (but you can have a different opinion) Oh there is no reason to one over the other, I had just figured I know Nethermind is C# and has people with a background in other C languages so it may be easier for them to use Although Rust's safety and similar perf may end up being a better fit Okay good to know Make sure to check out Kev's Hackmd's above in this channel btw, I found them very helpful and ofc Python impl, EIP, libraries etc I need one specifically in C++ so I need to that regardless Okay, yes sure
